task.title: Atomically rebind owner and reviewer across fallback dead ends

scope.owned_layer: Supervisor assignment-pair planning, configured/preferred fallback traversal, canonical assignment compare-and-swap, and regression evidence.
scope.not_changing: Account or quota groups, provider readiness policy, global reviewer bans, catalog contracts, product tasks, canonical JSON by hand, live runtime state, or rollout.

contract.pair_planning: Every automatic owner fallback is evaluated together with an independent reviewer candidate before canonical mutation; the incumbent reviewer may become owner when another viable reviewer completes the pair.
contract.candidate_order: Direct configured fallbacks retain declaration order, task-preferred lanes follow, and discovered mapping edges are traversed breadth-first with case-insensitive de-duplication.
contract.bounded_cycles: Traversal is bounded by the finite unique candidate names and terminates when mappings contain cycles such as Antigravity -> Codex2 -> Antigravity.
contract.atomic_persistence: The canonical lock compares expected owner, reviewer, and status before assigning both fields in the same governed write.
contract.shared_consumers: Mainline normalization, helper claim dispatch, and worker-failure owner fallback consume plan_task_assignment_pair.
contract.fail_closed: Catalog-locked tasks and tasks without a viable distinct pair are not mutated.
contract.identity_boundary: Reviewer independence remains distinct agent identity; Codex/Codex2 mutual review is allowed and no account/quota-group rule is added.

reproduce_23_stranded_tasks.result: All 23 unavailable-Antigravity/Codex2-reviewer todo tasks plan and persist Codex2 owner with Codex reviewer.
